PROPOSAL DESCRIPTION: We propose installation of 3 permanent tie-downs for single-engine aircraft in a dedicated aircraft parking area adjacent to the pilot campground on the SW side of S69. The site is a 250’ x 70’ grassy area off the end of Runway 4 centered at approximately 46° 57’ 04.36” N x 112° 39’ 23.07” W; a dirt taxiway currently leads to this existing tie-down parking area. Construction will be of in-ground concrete anchors for transient aircraft parking. The 7:1 Transitional Surface plane defined in Part 77 reaches a height of 12.5 ft at the fence line; thus  parked aircraft tails will likely penetrate the plane while using the parking area. However  they do not penetrate the plane made by the trees just outside of the fence.  Aircraft using the space will be transient and thus will not present a permanent structure or obstacle  but may be commonly present  especially during the summer months when the campground receives more frequent use. No permanent structure will be present above ground level. Permanent tie-down installation will help to maintain consistent aircraft orientation while parked. Anchors will be flush with the ground  but aircraft  when parked and vehicles and personnel during the short construction period will  in some cases  exceed the transitional surface plane. The extent to which this occurs will vary with the type of aircraft parked  but again  will be below the plane created by surrounding trees at the airport perimeter. This proposal also provides for the estimated 3-day construction period  which may include digging equipment  concrete-pouring equipment  vehicles  and related personnel in the project area. The included map figures show the location of the project site relative to the runway surface.

PROPOSAL DESCRIPTION: The terrain is very hilly in the Shelton area with extensive old tree growth. With the primary area of interest being to the East towards SEATAC and the 16 and 34 Approach corridors as well as other terminal operations in this airspace. The larger tower heights are being selected due to the vegetation heights in the area  which the RCAS and other systems MITRE uses do not see. The only system that accounts for vegetation are LIDAR based systems. With the prevalence of tree growth and close in hillsides in the Shelton area. It is important to evaluate the close in Eastern view covering the greatest amount of the target terminal area  the predominance of the maximum tree height being 60’to 80’
LOCATION DESCRIPTION: The proposed location of this tower would be roughly 850 ft west of highway 101 and 200 ft south of anderson way in an open plot on airport property

STRUCTURE NAME: Joint Base Lewis McChord Elevated Tank
PROPOSAL DESCRIPTION: This proposal involves the construction of one elevated steel water storage tank  with a capacity of 1 000 000 gallons  on a 2.2-acre site located at the southeast corner of South Gate Road and Lincoln Boulevard SW  within McChord Field at Joint Base Lewis-McChord (JBLM)  Lakewood  Pierce County  WA. The tank is designed to meet a water system overflow elevation of 440 feet above mean sea level (MSL) and maintain a minimum pressure of 30 psi throughout the distribution network. The approximate center coordinates of the site are 47.0720° N  122.2953° W  and the approximate ground elevation is 324 feet MSL.nThe elevated tank will be supported by a steel pedestal and concrete foundation  with structure height and final site grading to be provided in detailed construction documents. No antennas  microwave equipment  overhead wires  or radiating equipment are part of this proposal. This FAA notification is required due to the anticipated structure height and the proximity to McChord Field runways. All design and construction will meet applicable federal  state  and military standards  including any stormwater pollution prevention and restoration requirements.
LOCATION DESCRIPTION: The proposed site is located within McChord Field at Joint Base Lewis-McChord (JBLM) in Lakewood  Pierce County  Washington. It occupies approximately 2.2 acres at the southeast corner of South Gate Road and Lincoln Boulevard SW.  The site lies within the controlled grounds of McChord Air Force Base and is in close proximity to the airfield and associated military facilities. The nearest existing building is the McChord Child Development Center (CDC)  which is located adjacent to the site. This site is also bordered by the McChord AFB Museum  baseball fields  a recycling facility  convenience store  and other public amenities.

PROPOSAL DESCRIPTION: This The pole line on the west side of Grassy Mountain sits entirely on BLM property. It is overdue for maintenance; CLP intends to replace the entire line with a better engineered solution to resolve multiple issues.  Of the ~60 poles  CLP crews can (and are  right now) replace ~30 without air support. The remaining 30 poles will be replaced a contractor. That contractor (still undetermined) will air lift air compressors to key locations. Crews will excavate for the new pole line using those air compressors and air powered tools. CLP has determined that using air support is the least expensive option that simultaneously maintains power to the assets atop the mountain.
LOCATION DESCRIPTION: Power pole replacement from Grassy Mountain to Utah Test and Training Range.
